cultural.vision_reason: An antler amulet carved in classic Tlingit style as a killer whale, pierced for suspension and worn as personal adornment—consistent with Tlingit-made jewelry/amulets.

physical.title: amulet
physical.summary: Amulet, made from a piece of antler from a young deer, curved, and with three small tines, elegantly carved in the form of a killer whale[?], one tine acting as as the dorsal fin, two further tines as the tail. The creature is not carved with a mouth as such, but is carved with a low relief head, set in a rectangle, at the tip, in classic Tlingit style, this is followed by two large eyes, over a partial mouth and flipper on the underside with, two flippers just in front of the dorsal fin. The tip of the nose is pierced for suspension, has a piece commercial[?] string through it, with also a fragment of cotton shirt [?]. The whole artefact is dark brown, well patinated and clearly of age when collected. Attached is a printed pre-acquisition label: '154'.
